These days even the Republicans don't like the GOP party
The most interesting thing about the survey is the GOP has a lower favorable opinion now than it did in 2009 after the economic crash and 2 wars.

While an anecdotal generalization, most young republicans I know are a lot more moderate and open minded on several social issues. I left the party because I don't feel represented by the Baby Boomers and Gen X. I went Libertarian but I consider myself to be pretty moderate.

I think as were confronted with more and more issues, the moderates and younger generation are having to confront them with a more open mind.

You don't have to change your viewpoint, but you have to be able to look at it objectively. The GOP Good Ol' Boys refuse to do that, and that's what's hurting the party.

This isn't really surprising. What I don't understand is how the GOP party can be this unpopular, all of the GOP candidates keep doubling down on their unpopular stances, and yet they still are doing well in polls against the Democratic candidates. With this many candidates running you would think one of the parties would by luck get one that has broad appeal.

That Vox finds this surprising is an indictment of Vox's political sagacity.

Remember Porkbusters, the small government movement from the Bush II era that wanted to cut pork when the Republicans had majorities in the house and senate as well as the presidency? The gentry GOP has been ignoring the wishes of Main Street Republican voters for decades. The Tea Party was as much opposed to the GOP leadership as much as they were the Democrats.
